correctness.rationale: A is an associative skew group presentation with pm normal forms; J=(x-1)A is two-sided and has powers (x-1)^kA of dimensions m(p-k). The separable cyclic quotient proves J is exactly the Jacobson radical. All roots beta of Y^m-a satisfy beta^q=c beta, so their Frobenius orbits have uniform length d. The roots form m/d orbits; the primitive idempotents lift in the y-subalgebra, and y acting on the kth radical layer of Ae_j scales each root by r^k. The scale action is transitive of order h, giving one simple factor per layer and the Cartan formula I_h+(p-1)/h 11^T. Twelve exact prime-field examples, with exhaustive basis associativity for dimension <=20, corroborate the proof. No experiment is substituted for a proof in untested sizes.

originality.rationale: The 2026 source treats semisimple coefficient characteristic ell != p and explicitly leaves the modular case outside its Wedderburn theorem. Wallace 1970 already covers the general radical phenomenon, and cyclic-defect theory covers split analogues; neither is claimed as new. The surviving contribution is the complete finite-field scalar-twist/Galois-order classification of projective layers and Cartan matrices, including nonsplit twist classes and all prime powers. The closest relevant full texts and actual database queries produced no stronger coverage; publication-index omissions remain a risk.

value.rationale: The field-characteristic change from the 2026 semisimple classification to modular p is a natural omitted structural regime. The result simultaneously computes the nilpotent filtration, the cohomology-class-dependent number and degrees of simples, the uniserial projective-layer cycle, all Cartan entries/eigenvalues and all attainable cocycle strata. Example p=7,m=6 has four different simple-count profiles h=6,3,2,1 as a varies. These invariants are useful for modular projective representation and Morita-type distinctions. Known radical identification alone would not have sufficient value; the arithmetic representation-type classification is the substantive part.
